title: Corporate actions, IPOs and the primary market
objectives: Describe how an IPO, rights issue and buyback work.
Explain how dividends, bonus and splits change the share price and count.
body_md:
## Primary market routes

| Route | What happens |
|---|---|
| **IPO** | Fresh issue and/or offer for sale (OFS) to the public, usually by **book building** with a price band |
| **Rights issue** | Existing holders get the right to buy more at a discount |
| **QIP / preferential** | Private placement to institutions or chosen investors |
| **Buyback** | Company repurchases its own shares (tender or open market) |

In a book-built IPO the **cap of the price band cannot exceed 120% of the floor**. Allotment follows the investor-category quotas in the offer document (retail, non-institutional, QIB). Listing follows within a few days of issue close (**T+3**, verify).

## Corporate actions and their price effect

- **Dividend:** cash paid out. Price falls by about the dividend on the **ex-date**. Under T+1 the ex-date and record date fall together (verify).
- **Bonus:** free extra shares (1:1 doubles the count). Price adjusts down; **total value is unchanged**.
- **Split:** face value is cut (₹10 to ₹2 gives 5 shares for 1). Value unchanged, liquidity often improves.
- **Rights:** dilutes holders who do not subscribe.
- **Buyback:** reduces share count, can lift EPS.
- **Merger / demerger:** swap ratio decides value.

## Why analysts care

Always adjust historical prices, EPS and DPS for splits and bonuses before computing growth or multiples. Unadjusted series show false crashes.

> **Exam tip:** Bonus and split change the share count and price, not the market capitalisation.
example: A stock at ₹1,200 announces a 1:1 bonus. Holders with 100 shares now have 200 shares; the price adjusts to about ₹600. Value stays ₹1,20,000.
say: Corporate actions change the share count, so I adjust the history before comparing.
A bonus is not free value; the price adjusts.
never: A bonus issue makes the investor richer.
A split changes the company value.

check.q: A 1:1 bonus issue does what to the market capitalisation?
check.why: More shares at a proportionately lower price: value is unchanged.

check.q: In a book-built IPO the price band cap can be at most:
check.why: ICDR limits the cap to 120% of the floor price.

check.q: A split from face value ₹10 to ₹2 gives how many shares per old share?
